The API now validates the stored ResolvedWorkspaceProjection against the exact generated Workstream scope before returning it. Desktop uses the generated projectionGet method and registry-owned GET/path metadata, validates the generated projection, rejects foreign contribution authority, and retains per-authority projection revision/layout/cursor watermarks so stale responses fail closed without changing Core-owned eligibility or layout composition.

implementation: The API requires mission_canvas:read, parses the generated Workstream query and subordinate identity values, reads the latest projection keyed by the exact Workstream authority, and invokes Core's ResolvedWorkspaceProjection::validate_scope before serializing the response. A tampered or mismatched stored projection is blocked rather than adopted.

The Desktop transport resolves the HTTP method and path from the generated operation registry, sends the exact Workstream authority and supplied permission/capability metadata, validates the generated ResolvedWorkspaceProjection, and compares top-level and eligible-contribution authority without resolving candidates, layout, or semantic content locally.

Projection responses are watermarked per complete Workstream authority. Regressed projection revision, layout revision, or comparable durable cursor is rejected while cursor namespaces remain distinct; a foreign Workstream, subordinate authority, missing focused-surface authority, malformed response, denied permission, or unavailable operation cannot reach the renderer.

The hostile generated Desktop consumer proves projectionGet, exact GET/path/query/header transport, Core-owned empty-contribution omission, foreign top-level and nested contribution scope, missing request/response authority, stale projection/layout/cursor responses, denied permission, unavailable operation, and invalid response handling.

negative_cases.foreign_workstream: The API validates the stored projection against the exact query scope, while Desktop rejects a response whose top-level Workstream or eligible-contribution Workstream differs from the request.
negative_cases.missing_authority: The generated transport rejects a request without Workstream identity before HTTP, and generated response validation rejects a projection without Workstream authority. A focused surface also requires matching Attachment and WorkSurface authority.
negative_cases.stale_revision_cursor: Desktop retains independent per-authority projection and layout watermarks and rejects projection_revision, layout_revision, or same-namespace durable cursor regressions without updating the accepted watermark.
negative_cases.unavailable_capability: projection.get has no separate required capability in the generated descriptor; therefore no capability is inferred or minted locally. An unavailable/unknown generated operation is rejected before HTTP, and supplied capability metadata remains transport-owned for the API boundary.
negative_cases.permission_denied: The generated operation declares mission_canvas:read; the hostile consumer proves a 403 response is surfaced as a typed transport failure when that permission is absent.
negative_cases.empty_or_ineligible_contribution: The valid exact-Workstream fixture contains an empty Work Rail candidate only in omission_diagnostics; Desktop verifies that it is absent from eligible contributions and layout and does not invent a replacement panel.
negative_cases.invalid_response: Generated structural validation plus projection authority/watermark checks reject missing Workstream, missing contribution authority, foreign nested authority, invalid focused-surface authority, malformed contribution collections, empty cursors, and stale responses.
negative_cases.local_inference: No CWD, tab, latest record, project-root/continuity shortcut, client-side candidate search, eligibility resolver, or layout resolver is used. Core remains the sole composition authority and Desktop consumes the canonical projection.
